diagnostic_evidence.quote: U^{n+1}_i = (1 - s_j) U^*_i + s_j \sum_{k \in W_i} w_{i,k} \hat{Q}^*_k

issues.failure_explanation: The proof decomposes the time step as pre-merge, finite-volume update on the merged mesh, and blended redistribution. However, the UM-SRD definition and Algorithm alg:added-1 perform the finite-volume update on the original cut-cell mesh first, then aggregate and blend; no pre-merge before the update is present. Thus the theorem proves TVD for a different scheme. Moreover, actual UM-SRD is not TVD under the stated CFL: take α=0.1, ν=aΔt/h=1, initial values 0,0,1,0 around the small cell. Initial TV=2; after one UM-SRD step with s≈1, TV≈3.8>2. So the theorem's claim is false.

failure_location.quote: Pre-merge: apply $S_j$ to map $U^n$ to neighborhood averages $Q^{n,-1}$ (lifted to the original mesh).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either modify the algorithm to include the pre-merge stage before the finite-volume update and prove TVD for that scheme, or prove TVD for the actual UM-SRD operator under a different CFL condition. No complete source-supported repair is identified for the stated theorem as written.
issues.overall_effect: The central TVD guarantee for UM-SRD is invalid; the algorithm's claim to inherit TVD and the paper's stability claims based on it are unsupported.
issues.title: TVD theorem proves a different algorithm and is false for UM-SRD

issues.failure_explanation: The volume-weighted average of values over a full cell of volume h and a small cell of volume αh is (U_{j-1}+α U_j)/(1+α), not (1-α)U_{j-1}+α U_j. The latter is a convex combination with incorrect weights. The error propagates to the SRD redistribution formula, the steady-state change formula, and the error-accumulation corollary; the local-consistency proof's algebra is also wrong, although the final O(h) bound may survive with different constants.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the incorrect simplification everywhere with the correct weighted average (U_{j-1}+α U_j)/(1+α) and update downstream constants and formulas.
issues.overall_effect: The specific numerical values and formulas for SRD's steady-state modification and error accumulation are incorrect; the local-consistency proof contains a false algebraic step.
issues.title: Incorrect simplification of the volume-weighted neighborhood average
issues.why_classification: The error is a local algebraic correction; it changes constants and specific formulas but preserves the order conclusions and the overall structure of the affected results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For a smooth exact solution $u$ and a first-order consistent scheme, $B(u^n) = u^{n+1} + \mathcal{O}(h)$

issues.failure_explanation: Under the CFL condition Δt=O(h), the one-step error B(u^n)-u^{n+1} of the first-order upwind scheme is O(h^2), not O(h). For p=1, the perturbation s_j(S_j-I)B(u^n) is also O(h^2), so it is the same order as the base one-step error, not higher-order. The proposition's claim of a higher-order term for all p≥1 is therefore false; it holds only for p>1.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The base scheme is the first-order upwind finite volume method with flux \begin{equation} F(U_i, U_{i+1}) = a U_i, \qquad a > 0. \end{equation}
Thus, if $U^n_{j-1} \neq U^n_j$, then $U^{n+1} \neq U^n$ even though the finite-volume update is zero.

issues.failure_explanation: For first-order upwind with a>0, the update U^*_i = U_i - (aΔt/Δx_i)(U_i-U_{i-1}) vanishes for all i only if U_i=U_{i-1} for all i, so the only steady states are constant. Hence the scenario U_{j-1}≠U_j in the proposition cannot occur. The proposition does not establish that SRD fails to preserve non-constant steady states of the base scheme; in fact, SRD preserves constant states. Experiment 6 forces U^*=U for a non-steady state, which is not a valid time step of the base scheme.

failure_location.quote: Let $U^n$ be a steady state for the base finite-volume scheme, i.e., $U^*_i = U^n_i$ for all $i$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either change the model to one that admits non-constant steady states (e.g., add a source term or set a=0), or restate the proposition as a forced-zero-update redistribution property rather than a steady-state property.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed limitation of standard SRD regarding steady-state preservation is not demonstrated for the analyzed model, undermining a central motivation for UM-SRD's shut-off mechanism. The UM-SRD zero-update property itself remains true.
issues.title: Non-constant steady states do not exist for the 1D upwind model
issues.why_classification: The repair requires changing the model or abandoning the advertised steady-state contrast between SRD and UM-SRD; a central motivating claim is invalidated for the analyzed setting.

issues.failure_explanation: For any finite nonzero ΔU_max, η_j = ΔU_max/(ε+ΔU_max) is strictly less than 1, not equal to 1. It is only approximately 1 when ΔU_max is much larger than ε. Also η_j=0 requires ΔU_max=0 exactly, not merely updates at machine precision. Thus the claim that the normalized indicator is effectively binary for any nonzero update is false for updates comparable to or smaller than ε.

failure_location.quote: By construction, $\eta_j = 0$ if and only if all updates in $M_j$ are at machine precision, and $\eta_j \approx 1$ whenever any cell in $M_j$ has a nonzero update.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the equality with the correct inequality η_j<1 and clarify that η_j≈1 only when ΔU_max≫ε, and that exact shut-off requires exactly zero updates.
issues.overall_effect: The analysis of the normalized implementation overstates its activation for very small updates; the exact shut-off property (s=0 when updates are exactly zero) remains true.
issues.title: Normalized indicator does not equal one for any nonzero update
